neighbors.establishing_passage: The study trained an NCCT deep-learning biomarker of lesion age and compared it with relative intensity equivalent to NWU.
The paper automated mirrored-region NWU using baseline CTP core and follow-up lesion segmentation.
A 390-patient study stratified CTP core thresholds by NWU and evaluated final infarct and long-term outcome.
PerfU-Net is explicitly symmetry-aware and jointly exploits infarcted and healthy hemispheres.
The DL core/penumbra method was compared with clinical contralateral-relative threshold software.
Contralateral-normalized relative CBF was evaluated as the optimal CTP core definition.
The study estimated distinct gray- and white-matter perfusion thresholds for infarction.
Patient-tailored perfusion transformations improved tissue-fate prediction and included separate GM/WM modeling.
An Attention U-Net predicted follow-up infarct core from multiple CTP maps and baseline CT.
Patlak permeability maps from first-pass CTP showed elevated PS in ischemia and association with hemorrhagic transformation.
Nonlinear-regression relative PS outperformed standard Patlak estimates for hemorrhagic-transformation discrimination.
A spatio-temporal network predicted treatment-specific lesion outcome directly from raw 4D CTP.
CTA attenuation increase quantified thrombus perviousness and associated with recanalization, outcome, and smaller infarct volume.
CTA-index was proposed as a simplified thrombus-perviousness measure with outcome-prediction utility.
A seven-trial pooled analysis related perviousness to functional outcome, infarct volume, and EVT treatment effect.
Registration quantified head motion during CTP; moderate or severe motion occurred in roughly one quarter of patients.
Motion severity was characterized and associated with NIHSS, age, and onset time.
Phantom motion altered automated RAPID core, penumbra, and mismatch estimates.
The study evaluated perfusion-CT definitions of infarct core and penumbra centered on CBV physiology.
Relative CBF was found preferable to CBV as a core-defining CTP parameter.
A deep model predicted final infarct from native CTP and treatment metadata and reported input/metadata ablations.
Acute infarct topology was related to lesion volume and neurological severity on MRI.
Spatial-temporal processing of raw 4D CTP improved lesion-outcome prediction.
Deep generative perfusion-deficit mapping modeled disrupted-perfusion topology to localize NIHSS substrates.
